question.problem: Consider the Diophantine equation $9x+11y=6.$ The integer pair $(\overset{∼}{x},\overset{∼}{y})$ is the solution with the greatest possible negative value of $y.$ What is the value of $\overset{∼}{y}?$
question.worked_solution:
We have the linear Diophantine equation

$$
ax+by=c
$$

where $a=9,$ $b=11,$ and $c=6.$ We're given that the equation has solutions.

Notice that our equation can't be solved for either of the two variables using integer coefficients. So, let's find the linear representation of $\text{gcd}(9,11)$ using the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}11 & = & 9\cdot 1 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 9 & = & 2\cdot 4 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =11-9 \\ 1 & =9-2\cdot 4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =9-2\cdot 4 \\  & =9-4(11-9) \\  & =9\cdot 5+11\cdot (-4).\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that $d=\text{gcd}(a,b)=1$ and

$$
9\cdot 5+11\cdot (-4)=1.
$$

Multiplying this equation by $6,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9\cdot 5+11\cdot (-4) & =1 \\ 9\cdot 5\cdot 6+11\cdot (-4)\cdot 6 & =6 \\ 9\cdot 30+11\cdot (-24) & =6,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that $(x,y)=(30,-24)$ is a solution to our Diophantine equation.

Now, the general solution is

$$
(30+\frac{b}{d}t,\,-24-\frac{a}{d}t)=(30+11t,\,-24-9t),
$$

where $t=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…\,.$

The greatest possible negative value of $y=-24-9t$ is attained when $t=-2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\overset{∼}{y}=-24-9\cdot (-2)=-6.
$$
